   797→        >>> gdf
   798→            col1     geometry

   800→        1  name2  POINT (2 1)

   802→        >>> gdf.to_json()
   803→        '{"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [{"id": "0", "type": "Feature", \
   804→"properties": {"col1": "name1"}, "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [1.0,\
   805→ 2.0]}}, {"id": "1", "type": "Feature", "properties": {"col1": "name2"}, "geometry"\
   806→: {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [2.0, 1.0]}}], "crs": {"type": "name", "properti\
   807→es": {"name": "urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::3857"}}}'

   903→            if the index is just arbitrary row numbers.

  1610→              checking the identity of the index)

  1678→            object is provided, the values in the list are treated as categorical

  1683→            with each group. Passed to pandas `groupby.agg` method.

  1685→

  1694→            particular level or levels.

  1697→        sort : bool, default True
  1698→            Sort group keys. Get better performance by turning this off.
  1699→            Note this does not influence the order of observations within
  1700→            each group. Groupby preserves the order of rows within each group.
  1701→
  1702→            .. versionadded:: 0.9.0

  1704→            This only applies if any of the groupers are Categoricals.
  1705→            If True: only show observed values for categorical groupers.
  1706→            If False: show all values for categorical groupers.
  1707→

  1711→            together with row/column will be dropped. If False, NA
  1712→            values will also be treated as the key in groups.
  1713→

  1717→            which is used by `dissolve`. In particular, `numeric_only` may be
  1718→            supplied, which will be required in pandas 2.0 for certain aggfuncs.

  1723→        GeoDataFrame
  1724→

  1726→        --------
  1727→        >>> from shapely.geometry import Point
  1728→        >>> d = {
  1729→        ...     "col1": ["name1", "name2", "name1"],
  1730→        ...     "geometry": [Point(1, 2), Point(2, 1), Point(0, 1)],
  1731→        ... }
  1732→        >>> gdf = geopandas.GeoDataFrame(d, crs=4326)
  1733→        >>> gdf
  1734→            col1     geometry
  1735→        0  name1  POINT (1 2)
  1736→        1  name2  POINT (2 1)
  1737→        2  name1  POINT (0 1)
  1738→
  1739→        >>> dissolved = gdf.dissolve('col1')
  1740→        >>> dissolved  # doctest: +SKIP
  1741→                                geometry
  1742→        col1
  1743→        name1  MULTIPOINT ((0 1), (1 2))
  1744→        name2                POINT (2 1)
  1745→
  1746→        See also
  1747→        --------
  1748→        GeoDataFrame.explode : explode multi-part geometries into single geometries
  1749→
  1750→        """
  1751→
  1752→        if by is None and level is None:
  1753→            by = np.zeros(len(self), dtype="int64")
  1754→
  1755→        groupby_kwargs = {
  1756→            "by": by,
  1757→            "level": level,
  1758→            "sort": sort,
  1759→            "observed": observed,
  1760→            "dropna": dropna,
  1761→        }
  1762→
  1763→        # Process non-spatial component
  1764→        data = self.drop(labels=self.geometry.name, axis=1)
  1765→        with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as record:
  1766→            aggregated_data = data.groupby(**groupby_kwargs).agg(aggfunc, **kwargs)
  1767→        for w in record:
  1768→            if str(w.message).startswith("The default value of numeric_only"):
  1769→                msg = (
  1770→                    f"The default value of numeric_only in aggfunc='{aggfunc}' "
  1771→                    "within pandas.DataFrameGroupBy.agg used in dissolve is "
  1772→                    "deprecated. In pandas 2.0, numeric_only will default to False. "
  1773→                    "Either specify numeric_only as additional argument in dissolve() "

  1779→                # other warnings from pandas should be passed through
  1780→                # TODO this is not an ideal approach
  1781→                warnings.showwarning(
  1782→                    w.message, w.category, w.filename, w.lineno, w.file, w.line
  1783→                )

  1786→

  1788→        def merge_geometries(block):
  1789→            merged_geom = block.union_all()
  1790→            return merged_geom

  1799→        aggregated = aggregated_geometry.join(aggregated_data)

  1802→        if not as_index:
  1803→            aggregated = aggregated.reset_index()

  1807→    # overrides the pandas native explode method to break up features geometrically
  1808→    def explode(self, column=None, ignore_index=False, index_parts=None, **kwargs):
  1809→        """
  1810→        Explode multi-part geometries into multiple single geometries.
  1811→
  1812→        Each row containing a multi-part geometry will be split into
  1813→        multiple rows with single geometries, thereby increasing the vertical
  1814→        size of the GeoDataFrame.
  1815→
  1816→        Parameters
  1817→        ----------
  1818→        column : string, default None
  1819→            Column to explode. In the case of a geometry column, multi-part
  1820→            geometries are converted to single-part.
  1821→            If None, the active geometry column is used.
  1822→        ignore_index : bool, default False
  1823→            If True, the resulting index will be labelled 0, 1, …, n - 1,
  1824→            ignoring `index_parts`.
  1825→        index_parts : boolean, default True
  1826→            If True, the resulting index will be a multi-index (original
  1827→            index with an additional level indicating the multiple
  1828→            geometries: a new zero-based index for each single part geometry
  1829→            per multi-part geometry).
  1830→
  1831→        Returns
  1832→        -------
  1833→        GeoDataFrame
  1834→            Exploded geodataframe with each single geometry
  1835→            as a separate entry in the geodataframe.
  1836→
  1837→        Examples
  1838→        --------
  1839→
  1840→        >>> from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
  1841→        >>> d = {
  1842→        ...     "col1": ["name1", "name2"],
  1843→        ...     "geometry": [
  1844→        ...         MultiPoint([(1, 2), (3, 4)]),
  1845→        ...         MultiPoint([(2, 1), (0, 0)]),
  1846→        ...     ],
  1847→        ... }
  1848→        >>> gdf = geopandas.GeoDataFrame(d, crs=4326)
  1849→        >>> gdf
  1850→            col1               geometry
  1851→        0  name1  MULTIPOINT ((1 2), (3 4))
  1852→        1  name2  MULTIPOINT ((2 1), (0 0))
  1853→
  1854→        >>> exploded = gdf.explode(index_parts=True)
  1855→        >>> exploded
  1856→              col1     geometry
  1857→        0 0  name1  POINT (1 2)
  1858→          1  name1  POINT (3 4)
  1859→        1 0  name2  POINT (2 1)
  1860→          1  name2  POINT (0 0)
  1861→
  1862→        >>> exploded = gdf.explode(index_parts=False)
  1863→        >>> exploded
  1864→            col1     geometry
  1865→        0  name1  POINT (1 2)
  1866→        0  name1  POINT (3 4)
  1867→        1  name2  POINT (2 1)
  1868→        1  name2  POINT (0 0)
  1869→
  1870→        >>> exploded = gdf.explode(ignore_index=True)
  1871→        >>> exploded
  1872→            col1     geometry
  1873→        0  name1  POINT (1 2)
  1874→        1  name1  POINT (3 4)
  1875→        2  name2  POINT (2 1)
  1876→        3  name2  POINT (0 0)
  1877→
  1878→        See also
  1879→        --------
  1880→        GeoDataFrame.dissolve : dissolve geometries into a single observation.
  1881→
  1882→        """
  1883→
  1884→        # If no column is specified then default to the active geometry column
  1885→        if column is None:
  1886→            column = self.geometry.name
  1887→        # If the specified column is not a geometry dtype use pandas explode
  1888→        if not isinstance(self[column].dtype, GeometryDtype):
  1889→            return super().explode(column, ignore_index=ignore_index, **kwargs)
  1890→
  1891→        if index_parts is None:
  1892→            if not ignore_index:
  1893→                warnings.warn(
  1894→                    "Currently, index_parts defaults to True, but in the future, "
  1895→                    "it will default to False to be consistent with Pandas. "
  1896→                    "Use `index_parts=True` to keep the current behavior and "
  1897→                    "True/False to silence the warning.",
  1898→                    FutureWarning,
  1899→                    stacklevel=2,
  1900→                )
  1901→            index_parts = True
  1902→
  1903→        exploded_geom = self.geometry.reset_index(drop=True).explode(index_parts=True)
  1904→
  1905→        df = self.drop(self._geometry_column_name, axis=1).take(
  1906→            exploded_geom.index.droplevel(-1)
  1907→        )
  1908→        df[exploded_geom.name] = exploded_geom.values
  1909→        df = df.set_geometry(self._geometry_column_name).__finalize__(self)
  1910→
  1911→        if ignore_index:
  1912→            df.reset_index(inplace=True, drop=True)
  1913→        elif index_parts:
  1914→            # reset to MultiIndex, otherwise df index is only first level of
  1915→            # exploded GeoSeries index.
  1916→            df = df.set_index(
  1917→                exploded_geom.index.droplevel(
  1918→                    list(range(exploded_geom.index.nlevels - 1))
  1919→                ),
  1920→                append=True,
  1921→            )
  1922→
  1923→        return df

import json
import pytest

import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import Point


def build_sample_gdf(crs=None):
    data = {
        "prop": ["a", "b"],
        "geometry": [Point(1, 2), Point(2, 1)],
    }
    gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(data, index=[10, 11], crs=crs)
    return gdf


def normalize(obj):
    # Normalize tuples/lists by round-tripping through JSON
    return json.loads(json.dumps(obj))


def test_to_geo_method_exists_and_callable():
    gdf = build_sample_gdf()
    assert hasattr(gdf, "to_geo"), "GeoDataFrame should have a public to_geo method"
    assert callable(getattr(gdf, "to_geo")), "GeoDataFrame.to_geo should be callable"


def test_to_geo_basic_structure_and_types():
    gdf = build_sample_gdf()
    fc = gdf.to_geo()
    assert isinstance(fc, dict)
    assert fc.get("type") == "FeatureCollection"
    features = fc.get("features")
    assert isinstance(features, list)
    assert len(features) == len(gdf)

    # Check first feature contents
    f0 = features[0]
    assert f0.get("type") == "Feature"
    # geometry should be a dict with type Point and coordinates
    geom = f0.get("geometry")
    assert isinstance(geom, dict)
    assert geom.get("type") == "Point"
    coords = geom.get("coordinates")
    assert isinstance(coords, (list, tuple))
    assert len(coords) == 2
    # properties should include non-geometry columns
    props = f0.get("properties")
    assert isinstance(props, dict)
    assert props.get("prop") == gdf.iloc[0]["prop"]
    # id should be present by default and match the index
    assert f0.get("id") == str(gdf.index[0])


def test_show_bbox_behavior_true_and_false():
    gdf = build_sample_gdf()
    fc_with_bbox = gdf.to_geo(show_bbox=True)
    assert "bbox" in fc_with_bbox, "Top-level bbox should be present when show_bbox=True"
    assert isinstance(fc_with_bbox["bbox"], (list, tuple))
    assert len(fc_with_bbox["bbox"]) == 4
    for f in fc_with_bbox["features"]:
        assert "bbox" in f, "Feature-level bbox should be present when show_bbox=True"
        assert isinstance(f["bbox"], (list, tuple)) or f["bbox"] is None

    fc_no_bbox = gdf.to_geo(show_bbox=False)
    assert "bbox" not in fc_no_bbox, "Top-level bbox should be absent when show_bbox=False"
    for f in fc_no_bbox["features"]:
        assert "bbox" not in f, "Feature-level bbox should be absent when show_bbox=False"


def test_drop_id_behavior_true_and_false():
    gdf = build_sample_gdf()
    fc_no_id = gdf.to_geo(drop_id=True)
    assert all("id" not in f for f in fc_no_id["features"]), "drop_id=True should omit feature id"

    fc_with_id = gdf.to_geo(drop_id=False)
    assert all("id" in f for f in fc_with_id["features"]), "drop_id=False should include feature id"


def test_crs_handling_to_json_vs_to_geo():
    # Non-WGS84 CRS: to_json may include crs, to_geo must not include crs
    gdf = build_sample_gdf(crs="EPSG:3857")
    fc = gdf.to_geo()
    assert "crs" not in fc, "to_geo must not include 'crs' information"

    j = json.loads(gdf.to_json())
    assert "crs" in j, "to_json should include 'crs' for non-WGS84 CRS"


def test_no_crs_normalized_match_to_json_and_to_geo():
    # When no CRS is set, to_json and to_geo should match after normalization
    gdf = build_sample_gdf(crs=None)
    j = json.loads(gdf.to_json())
    fc_norm = normalize(gdf.to_geo())
    assert j == fc_norm, "Normalized to_json and to_geo outputs should match when CRS is None"
